chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), in
the hadith of Barirah that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to Aisha: 'Emancipate her, for the guardianship (wilayah) belongs to the one who emancipates.'

key_terms.أَعْتَقَ: A'taq, to have emancipated or freed.
key_terms.أَعْتِقِي: A'tiqi, the imperative command to emancipate or free.
key_terms.الْوَلَاءَ: Al-wala, the right of guardianship or manumission rights that accrue to the master who frees a slave.
key_terms.بَرِيرَةَ: Barirah, a specific slave woman whose emancipation case established this legal precedent.

ai.seo_question: Who has the right of guardianship over a freed slave according to the Prophet's instruction to Aisha?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Zurarah to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him), confirms the Prophet’s directive to Aisha regarding the freed slave Barira, establishing the legal principle of 'al-wala' (the right of manumission). In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a primary evidence that the patronage rights over a freed slave belong to the emancipator, a ruling that extends to inheritance and social obligations. The narration highlights the intersection of prophetic practice and Imami interpretation, reinforcing the continuity of legal authority from the Prophet to the Imams.

en.hubeali:
Muhamad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
regarding a Hadeeth of Bareyra that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said to Ayesha: ‘Emancipate, for the guardianship is for the one who emancipates’.
